evidence: ProfileScreen.handleSave() (:44-71) persists an edited first/last name ONLY to local device storage: `await SecureStore.setItemAsync(USER_KEY, JSON.stringify(updated))` (:61), then sets `savedAt = Date.now()` (:62) which drives a user-visible 'saved' confirmation (:124). The screen has ZERO API wiring — grep for useApi/apiRequest/useMutation in the file returns 0 matches; no addToQueue either.

There is NO backend profile-update call anywhere in the mobile app (repo-wide grep for users/me PATCH / updateProfile / updateUser outside push-token handlers finds nothing). The screen's own header docstring (:6) confirms this is a known stub: 'keys until the backend `PATCH /me` endpoint is wired in.'

Consequence: the name change never reaches the server and never syncs to web / other devices; it silently reverts the moment the cached User is overwritten by a login or a session-restore refetch (AuthContext writes USER_KEY on login), and is wiped by resetLocalData()/logout. Yet the user is shown a success state — a false-persistence data-integrity bug.

Cloud-landable (frontend-only) portion: either (a) route the edit through useOfflineSupport.addToQueue({endpoint:'/api/v1/users/me', method:'PATCH', body:{first_name,last_name}}) mirroring the ReportFault online/offline pattern so it actually syncs, or (b) at minimum stop presenting a device-only write as a persisted 'saved' profile update. Full server wiring additionally depends on the PATCH /me endpoint existing in api-server (verify before claiming the happy path).
